headline: GREENLAND MINES CLOSES SARFARTOQ: 34% OF GLOBAL NON-CHINA NdPr PRODUCTION IN ONE DEAL — $35M Acquisition Follows Government Approval; $2.05B NPV Project Enters Development Phase
snippet: Greenland Mines Ltd (Nasdaq: GRML) completed the acquisition of the Sarfartoq Nd-Pr Rare Earths Project in southwest Greenland on September 2, following Greenland Government approval. The $35-million deal ($20M cash + $15M securities) brings a project with a high-case pre-tax NPV of approximately US$2.05 billion into Greenland Mines' portfolio. At 2025 consumption levels, Sarfartoq's planned annual NdPr oxide output would represent approximately 34% of all NdPr oxide refined outside China — for each of the project's nine scheduled operating years. The 12.2-million-tonne resource processes at 1.4 Mt per annum at 1.32% TREO head grade. The company now moves to infill drilling, pilot-scale metallurgical test work, and mine engineering, with its technical team scheduled to return to site in September 2026 for drone-based magnetic surveys. Against the backdrop of China's November 10 export-control review deadline, a fully-acquired and government-approved NdPr project in a Western-aligned jurisdiction is as strategically significant as any announcement in the critical minerals space this year.

headline: SIBANYE 111% EBITDA JUMP FUNDS TWO NEW MINES — $340M Mt Lyell Copper (Tasmania) And Burnstone Gold (SA) Both Get Board Go-Ahead As H1 Revenue Hits R90bn
snippet: Sibanye-Stillwater reported September 2 that H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA more than doubled (+111%) to R31.8 billion as revenue climbed 64% to R90 billion — record performance the company immediately deployed into two mine approvals. Mt Lyell in Tasmania, Australia, received a positive investment decision: total capital of approximately US$340 million will restart the historic copper-gold mine near Queenstown, with first ore targeted for 2029 and steady-state production of 26,000 tonnes of copper, 16,000 oz of gold, and 116,000 oz of silver annually over a 23-year mine life. In parallel, the Burnstone gold project in South Africa received Board approval after a restated feasibility study: 130,000 oz of gold per year over a 25-year life from 2.7 million oz in reserves. With copper above US$6.59/lb and gold above US$4,300/oz, both investments clear their hurdle rates with margin — and the simultaneous approval of assets on two continents signals that Sibanye is using its exceptional cash generation cycle to build the base for its next decade of production.

headline: BRIXTON METALS HITS 12,386 g/t AG OVER 0.5m AT LANGIS — High-Grade Cobalt Camp Silver Surges In Hole 432 As 155-Hole 2026 Program Builds Toward Resource
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSXV: BBB) released September 2 results from additional drilling at its 100%-owned Langis Silver Project in the historic Cobalt, Ontario silver camp: hole LM-26-432 returned 1.00 metre at 6,199 g/t silver from 116.05 metres depth, including 0.50 metres at 12,386 g/t silver — the highest-grade individual interval recorded in the 2026 program to date. Results come from 33 holes added to the Shaft 6 area, bringing the 2026 total to 155 holes and 33,858 metres drilled. Langis sits inside one of the world's historically richest silver camps, where narrow-vein bonanza grades drove multiple previous mining cycles; at $64/oz silver and climbing structural deficits, the economics of defining an underground mineral resource in this camp have rarely been better. Brixton is systematically building the drill-hole density required for a resource estimate.

headline: GOLD ERASES ALL 2026 GAINS — Up Just 0.7% YTD, 20% Below January Record; Fed Hike Bets At 70% Drive Worst September Open Since 2018
snippet: Gold has effectively erased its entire 2026 price gain, settling around US$4,325/oz on September 2 — leaving the metal up just 0.7% for the year and trading approximately 20% below the record close of $5,419.83 reached on January 28. The catalyst was Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole posture driving market-implied September rate hike odds to 70% as oil above $90/bbl from Strait of Hormuz disruption adds an inflation channel that complicates any Fed pivot. Gold equities gave ground in parallel — Eldorado Gold down 3.2%, Agnico Eagle 2.8%, Equinox Gold 2.7%. For retail investors, the annual context matters: despite the correction, gold remains up 23% year-over-year and August closed as the sector's best month since 1994 for the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index (+33%). The question is whether Friday's non-farm payrolls number re-breaks the year's trend or accelerates the fall toward the critical $4,300 technical floor.

headline: ZAMBIA EYES $1.8 BILLION FROM SMALL-SCALE GOLD — ZCCM-IH Plans Ghana-Model Formalization; UAE Received $1.8B In Zambian Gold While Official Exports Were $128M
snippet: Zambia's state-controlled mining investor ZCCM Investments Holdings announced September 2 plans to formalize the country's artisanal and small-scale gold sector using Ghana's model — channeling purchases through a state-run gold board — to unlock more than US$1.8 billion in annual value that is currently leaking through unofficial channels. The arithmetic is stark: in 2023 the UAE imported approximately $1.8 billion of gold from Zambia while Hong Kong imported $108 million, yet Zambia's central bank recorded official gold exports of less than $128 million. The ZCCM CEO says increasing formal production to several hundred thousand ounces per year from 127,000 oz in 2025 is 'totally achievable.' Ghana's analogous formalization program generated approximately $10.8 billion in foreign exchange last year — evidence the model works at scale. For junior mining investors, the policy signal matters: formal gold sector investment in Zambia is becoming a government priority, reducing sovereign risk for permitted projects in a country sitting on material gold endowment adjacent to established copper mining infrastructure.

headline: GOLD STOCKS AT MOST BULLISH SEASONAL JUNCTURE IN YEARS — GoldSeek: 22 Of 25 Bull Years Have Asian Harvest Rally; Summer 2026 Anomaly Sets Up Powerful Autumn Entry
snippet: Adam Hamilton's latest GoldSeek analysis argues that gold stocks are at their most bullish seasonal juncture, at the transition from summer doldrums to autumn rally: in 22 of the last 25 bull-market years for gold, Asian harvest demand — followed by India's wedding season — drove outsized price gains beginning in late summer and extending through October. The piece identifies summer 2026's anomalous gold selling (driven by new Fed chair hawkishness fears and geopolitical noise) as the mechanism that has created an entry point rather than a trend break, with traders rebuilding positions ahead of seasonally strong demand. Gold has ranged from $257 in April 2001 to $5,394 in January 2026 over those 25 years; the pattern of autumn strength has persisted across radically different macro environments. For junior mining investors, the implication is that the current post-Warsh consolidation may be the setup for the sector's strongest seasonal move of the year.

headline: LITHIUM HITS 5-MONTH LOW AS CATL MINE RESTART AND BALD HILL, FINNISS RETURN SUPPLY — 30% Off May Highs; Structural Shift Or Temporary Reset?
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices slid to 156,500 CNY/T on September 2 — down 2.19% on the day and approximately 30% below their May 2026 multi-year highs — as multiple supply-side events converged: China's CATL secured clearance from security regulators to resume operations at its Jianxiawo lithium mine (expected to add up to 45,000 tonnes of lithium in H2), while Mineral Resources' Bald Hill operation (165,000 dmt/yr spodumene capacity) and Core Lithium's Finniss project both returned to production after multi-month suspensions. Crux Investor frames the central question as whether this is a structural oversupply signal or a temporary reset driven by a cluster of restarts. Against the bearish case: global battery demand grew 35%+ in 2025 to exceed 1.5 TWh and energy storage is emerging as a major structural demand driver independent of EV penetration. Against the bull case: lithium prices are still up approximately 100% year-on-year. The analysis is essential context for investors in ASX and TSXV lithium developers weighing project economics.

headline: OPUS ONE GOLD: ALL 2026 HOLES HIT TARGET OVER 800m STRIKE AT ZONE WEST NOYELL, QUEBEC — Definition Drilling Planned Below 300m As Project Data Density Builds
snippet: Opus One Gold Corp released September 2 all drill hole results from the 2026 program at its Zone West Noyell Gold Property in Matagami, Quebec: every drill hole intersected the main target over a strike length of 800 metres, with all holes returning significant gold results above the 300-metre level. The company now plans definition drilling across the target to increase drill-hole density and data density below 300 metres — the standard next step before commissioning a resource estimate on a consistently mineralised system. Zone West is located in the established Abitibi Greenstone Belt mining district, a world-class jurisdiction for gold discovery. The 100%-drill-hole hit rate over 800 metres of strike is the result that makes the next phase of work — deeper definition drilling — both technically justified and investor-fundable in a gold market above $4,300/oz.

headline: VISIONARY COPPER AND GOLD: PHASE 2 DRILL APPROVED AT PT. LEAMINGTON GOLD-COPPER-ZINC-SILVER VMS, NEWFOUNDLAND
snippet: Visionary Copper and Gold Mines Inc. (TSXV: VCG) received approval from the Newfoundland and Labrador Department of Energy and Mines on September 2 for its 2026 Phase 2 diamond drilling program at the Pt. Leamington VMS deposit — a gold-copper-zinc-silver volcanogenic massive sulphide system on Newfoundland's Avalon Peninsula. The Phase 2 program follows Phase 1 work that defined the VMS target's surface expression; Phase 2 diamond drilling will test the system at depth and along strike. VMS deposits in Newfoundland have a long discovery history and well-understood metallurgy; the Pt. Leamington multi-metal profile (Au-Cu-Zn-Ag) fits the polymetallic junior discovery narrative that has attracted investor attention in Atlantic Canada.

headline: UPSIDE GOLD EXCEEDS KENA GOLD-COPPER TARGET: 5,180m IN 19 HOLES VS 4,000m PLANNED — BC Resource Estimate Update Targeted Q1 2027
snippet: Upside Gold Corp. (CSE: UG) reported September 2 that it has completed its expanded 2026 diamond drilling program at the Kena Gold-Copper Project in southeastern British Columbia, drilling 5,180 metres in 19 diamond drill holes — surpassing the original 4,000-metre target by approximately 30%. Assay results from all 19 holes will be incorporated into an updated mineral resource estimate targeted for delivery in Q1 2027. Kena is a gold-copper porphyry target in a well-established mining district of southeastern B.C.; the expanded program beyond initial scope signals management confidence in the geology encountered during drilling. The Q1 2027 resource update will be the first formal quantification of the expanded dataset and will likely be the key catalyst for institutional interest in the project.
